children: HDFC Bank Limited Sponsored ADR (NSE:HDFCBANK) posted strong Q1 FY27 results and steady loan growth while the board proposed CEO candidates and governance changes as investors weigh valuation, RBI approval timing and potential strategic shifts amid volatile trading and heavy mutual fund buying.
Previous Week Recap
HDFCBANK CEO Candidates Submitted
: HDFCBANK submitted two CEO candidates and proposed three-year pay to the Reserve Bank of India before CEO Sashidhar Jagdishan’s term ends Oct 26, 2026; candidates include Kaizad Bharucha.
HDFC Bank ADR Q1 FY27 Highlights
: HDFC Bank ADR (HDFCBANK) Q1 FY27: gross advances +15.4% YoY, deposits up, PAT Rs190.6bn, NIM 3.26% (from 3.38% YoY), ROA 1.85%, ROE 13.8%.
HDFC Bank ADR Valuation Snapshot
: HDFC Bank ADR (HDFCBANK) trades at ~1.8x book, ~13.2x earnings, ROE 13.8%. Valuation sits below ICICI and Kotak; market pricing reflects uncertainty around restoring ROE toward 15%.
Nomura Keeps Buy On HDFC Bank ADR
: Nomura keeps Buy on HDFC Bank Sponsored ADR (HDFCBANK) with Rs 950 target, implying about 34% upside; internal CEO pick seen as continuity, external hire could trigger strategic reset.
Mutual Funds Buy HDFC ADR Shares
: In August, Indian mutual funds net bought HDFC Bank Limited Sponsored ADR (HDFCBANK) shares worth about ₹5,492 crore, making it one of the month’s top mutual fund purchases.
HDFCBANK Trading Amid RBI Wait
: HDFCBANK saw volatile trading as investors awaited RBI approval of CEO nominees. Traders noted pressure from foreign selling, oil-driven risk sentiment, and proximity to the 52-week high.
Ashika Sees Value, Growth Forecast
: Ashika Institutional's CEO sees HDFCBANK as attractively valued, forecasting 14–15% annual loan and profit growth; firm manages $200M+ in assets.
HDFC Bank ADR Board Expands
: HDFC Bank ADR (HDFCBANK): board approved adding one Whole-time Director, raising total to four plus the MD & CEO.
HDFCBANK Adds Institutional FCNRB Deposits
: HDFCBANK added institutional FCNRB deposits. Management says priority is sustaining stronger, steadier liability growth to bolster funding stability and support the bank’s funding profile.
Bahrain Court Dismisses Suits

: Bahrain High Civil Court dismissed all seven investor suits against HDFC Bank Limited Sponsored ADR (HDFCBANK) over Credit Suisse AT1 bonds, issuing final dismissals Sept. 9 and awarding legal costs.
